note: Wired+fixtured mobile screens the rendered-conformance guardrail does not yet ASSERT. A key here is NOT excused from parity — it is a written IOU with the concrete divergence named. Every wired+fixtured key must appear either as a committed tools/parity/expected/<key>.json that PASSES, or here with a real reason; a key in neither fails apps/mobile/src/parity/__tests__/rendered-conformance.test.tsx. Reasons must be >=40 characters and describe the blocker, not 'todo'. Reasons were written from the guardrail's own first run (2026-08-12) against every wired key, so this file doubles as the rendered-drift inventory: 7 keys conform, 32 do not.
recheck: node tools/parity/extract-expected.mjs  &&  pnpm --filter ./apps/mobile exec jest rendered-conformance

keys.LJ.force_update: App copy diverges from the mock verbatim: the mock draws 'Update to keep sending.', the app renders the role-neutral 'Update to keep using LyniaGo.' (app/force-update.tsx defends it in a comment, which carries no authority and has no docs/DESIGN-DEVIATIONS.md entry). Tracked as PXR-02; asserting it now would ratify the drift.
keys.LJ.history: Whole-screen divergence: the mock draws 'Your orders' over money-per-row order cards, the app renders 'Your trips' / 'Every parcel you've sent or delivered' over a different row grammar. 14 mock strings missing, 17 undrawn app strings — a structural alignment job, not an escape list.
keys.LJ.home_empty: Compose-screen copy diverges throughout ('Tap the map to drop your pickup pin' vs 'Tap the map to drop a pin for each address.') plus 7 more mock strings missing. Needs the send.tsx copy pass before it can be asserted.
keys.LJ.home_pins: The mock labels the two dropped pins 'A' and 'B' and draws its own sample addresses; the app renders neither the A/B pin letters nor matching addresses. 9 missing / 12 undrawn — pin-marker structure work, not a data escape.
keys.LJ.notifications: Notification copy is generated app-side with different grammar than the mock draws ('Your rider is on the way' vs 'Tendai M. is on the way'; 'Tapiwa is heading to the drop-off — track them live.' vs 'Arriving at pickup in about 6 min.'). 10 missing / 10 undrawn.
keys.LJ.otp: Two blockers: the fixture's phone renders as '0771234567' where the mock draws '+263 77 245 1180' (a display-format divergence, not sample data), and the app boots the resend COOLDOWN state ('Resend in 1:00') where the mock draws the ready state ('Didn't get it? Resend code'). The second needs a fixture that can stage a post-cooldown clock.
keys.LJ.profile: The mock's identity block draws the E.164 phone, a masked national ID and a 'NOT VERIFIED' chip; the app renders the local-format phone and none of the ID row, then adds four navigation rows the mock does not draw on this screen.
keys.LJ.settings: The mock draws a 'Chipo M.' / '+263 77 245 1180' identity row and an 'On' toggle value; the app renders the full name, local-format phone, and four rows the mock never draws ('Coming soon', 'Privacy notice', 'Delete account', an em-dash value).
keys.LJ.track_active: Status copy is a different vocabulary on each side (mock 'en route dropoff' vs app 'On the way to drop-off') and the order reference differs in shape ('Order 8f3a91c2' vs the fixture's UUID prefix). 14 missing / 18 undrawn — a tracking-screen alignment job.
keys.LJ.track_code: Same tracking-screen family as LJ.track_active: mock status vocabulary ('assigned') vs app ('Rider assigned'), plus 10 missing / 15 undrawn around the hand-off code block.
keys.RC.cart: The food_cart fixture stages a different restaurant and basket than the mock draws (mock: Sadza Republic, 'Arrives in 30–40 min · 10:11–10:21'; fixture: Gava's Kitchen). Aligning the fixture to the mock's basket is prerequisite work; 27 missing / 26 undrawn today.
keys.RC.checkout_cash: The food_checkout_cash fixture stages Gava's Kitchen where the mock draws Sadza Republic, and the mock's arrival-window line has no app counterpart. Fixture alignment first, then the remaining copy diff can be judged.
keys.RC.checkout_wallet: Same fixture-vs-mock restaurant mismatch as RC.checkout_cash, plus the mock's wallet line ('Pay the rider $15.50 when the food arrives') has no app equivalent. 10 missing / 16 undrawn.
keys.RC.delivered_rate: Time and money formatting diverge ('Delivered at 10:16' vs 'Delivered at 9:56 PM') and the fixture's totals differ from the mock's. Needs a fixture with a pinned delivery clock before the copy can be asserted.
keys.RC.list: The browse list is the largest gap in the wired set: 47 mock strings missing (sort pills, per-venue rating/ETA/fee, the mock's deliver-to) against 21 undrawn app strings. A full screen restructure, tracked separately from this guardrail.
keys.RC.menu: The mock draws a cover banner and logo image slot plus its own menu sample; the app stages Gava's Kitchen with initial-letter fallbacks. 17 missing / 17 undrawn — fixture photo/menu alignment then a copy pass.
keys.RC.orders: The app renders NONE of the mock's 14 strings and nothing of its own: with the food_orders fixture the screen paints an empty/loading shell in the jest environment. The fixture must stage the orders feed the mock draws before this key means anything.
keys.RC.pay_now: Order reference formats diverge (mock 'Order LG-4471' vs the app's UUID-derived 'Order 0A1B2C3D') and the fixture stages a different restaurant. 20 missing / 29 undrawn.
keys.RC.search: The mock draws a typed query ('sadza') with a 'PLACES' result section; the app renders the empty search hint. The fixture cannot yet stage a typed query into the screen's controlled input.
keys.RC.track_way: The mock's live map overlay draws single-glyph markers ('R', '•') and its own status grammar; the app renders 34 strings the mock does not draw. The heaviest map-screen gap in the set.
keys.RJ.bike_docs: Two fixture values ('ABZ 4417' vs the mock's 'ABZ 1234', ID mask '••••••' vs '631•••••••') plus an app copy branch: the mock draws 'checked by Didit', the app draws 'verified' with an extra 'Verified' badge. Mask format is an app-side divergence, not fixture data.
keys.RJ.job_assigned: Status vocabulary and fare grammar both diverge (mock 'assigned' / 'Agreed fare $3.00'; app 'Rider assigned' / a 'YOURS' badge the mock never draws). 18 missing / 26 undrawn.
keys.RJ.kyc_intro: The mock draws a short role-intro leaf; the app renders the full KYC FORM on the same route ('First name', field labels, 11 undrawn strings). A route/structure decision, not a copy fix.
keys.RJ.topup_amount: The mock draws a wallet top-up amount screen with a '‹ Wallet' back bar and amount presets; the app renders a support-contact screen instead ('Top up by contacting support'). 18 missing — the screens model different flows.
keys.RJM.account: Two fixture values (rider name, job count) plus two app copy divergences: the mock draws lowercase 'online' where the app renders 'Online', and 'Verified · expires Mar 2027' where the app renders 'Verified · view your documents'.
keys.RJM.active_food: The mock's active-job header and leg grammar ('Active job', 'Food · Sadza Republic → Belgravia') have no app counterpart ('Your job', 'Parcel collected'). 11 missing / 28 undrawn.
keys.RJM.board: The board renders its reconnecting banner in the jest environment (no socket) and its tag/section grammar differs from the mock's ('FOOD' section header, lowercase 'online'). 20 missing / 29 undrawn; needs a fixture that stages a connected socket.
keys.RJM.board_empty: Same socket problem as RJM.board — the app paints 'Reconnecting… your data may be a moment behind.' over the empty state — plus an empty-state copy divergence ('Parcels show up here…' vs the mock's 'You'll see parcels and food orders here…') and a 'Back to customer' row the mock does not draw.
keys.RJM.money: Balance figures come from the fixture and differ from the mock's, and the mock's '≈ 30 more jobs' runway line has no app counterpart while the app adds a long commission explainer the mock never draws.
keys.RJM.offer_food: The rider_food_offer fixture stages Nando's Avondale → Borrowdale where the mock draws Sadza Republic → Belgravia, and the app renders the collect amount as a bare '$13.00' where the mock draws 'Collect $15.50 for the kitchen' — a copy divergence hiding behind a fixture mismatch.
keys.RR.nav_rest: The mock draws map markers as single glyphs ('R', '•') and no SOS control; the app renders an SOS action and the fixture's restaurant. Marker structure work before this can be asserted.
keys.RR.offer_cash: The app renders the EXPIRED terminal ('That offer's gone') where the mock draws the live countdown offer ('NEW ORDER', '47s'): the offer fixture's expiry is in the past by the time jest mounts it. Needs a fixture with a pinned clock.
